rationale: This empirical remote-sensing, water/sediment sampling and survey study assesses land-use/land-cover transformation and wetland ecological risk in Halti Beel, Bangladesh. Although poor sanitation, unregulated land use and Environmental Conservation Rules (1997) water/sediment benchmarks are mentioned in the context of anthropogenic stressors on the wetland ecosystem, the study focuses on ambient wetland ecology and species vulnerability rather than domestic water or sanitation service access (E07).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings because the study assesses ambient wetland landscape transformation and ecological risk to species rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study investigates the ecological risk of Halti Beel, one of the significant parts of the largest wetland ecosystem of Bangladesh
An ecological risk model was developed using Landscape Ecological Risk Indexes (LERI) in Fragstats 4.2; risk zones were mapped, and risk levels were categorized from minimal to severe.
Most of the environmental and anthropogenic factors have strong connections with ecological risk and leave the current status of species highly vulnerable.
